preamble: Breathy-voiced /bʱ/ loses its oral closure and survives only as its breathy release, [ɦ] (written h). It became regular for intervocalic aspirates in Middle Indo-Aryan, especially Māhārāṣṭrī Prakrit, where kh, gh, th, dh, ph and bh all became h. It also occurs initially in the very frequent verb 'to be': Sanskrit bhavati > Prakrit hoi > Hindi honā.
phoneticEffects: Lenition, Debuccalization, Loss of Oral Closure

examples.note: Intervocalic bh > h is a regular Māhārāṣṭrī rule.
Via Ashokan Prakrit bhavati/hoti, Prakrit hoi and Old Hindi hoi.
Via Sauraseni Prakrit gahīra, where intervocalic bh had already become h.

sources: Pischel, R. (1900). Grammatik der Prākrit-Sprachen. Trübner. https://doi.org/10.1515/9783111700007
Masica, C. P. (1991). The Indo-Aryan Languages. Cambridge University Press. https://www.cambridge.org/9780521299442
